transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, it's been going on for a year now. I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is messing with my dad's lab results. They're changing them, or holding parts back. I know what I saw, you know? I draw blood for a living, I'm a phlebotomist, so I know how these things work. Which reminds me, we got this new centrifuge at work last week, and it's so loud. The old one was loud too, but this one has this high-pitched whine that just gets right into your teeth. My coworker Sarah says she doesn't hear it, but she listens to her music way too loud anyway. We went to that concert last month... anyway. No matter how many doctors or even my own family members tell me his numbers are fine, I know they're not. The chart doesn't match what I saw. It's just... it's really wearing me down.
During this past year, have you had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Energetic? No, not really. I've never had a time where I didn't need sleep or felt super energetic like that. I definitely need my sleep. I'm not one of those people who can just run on fumes. If I don't get my eight hours, my hands get shaky, and you can't have shaky hands when you're trying to hit a vein. 

I actually bought this new weighted blanket recently to help me get comfortable at night, because sometimes it takes me a while to drift off just thinking about my dad's situation. But the blanket is almost too heavy, you know? It traps all your body heat. I ordered it online and it took three weeks to get here. And when the delivery guy finally brought it, he just left it right in the middle of my driveway. Didn't even bring it up to the porch. Anyone could have just driven by and taken it. People steal packages all the time in my neighborhood now. My neighbor had a whole box of gardening supplies taken right off her front steps last Tuesday... anyway, what were we talking about? But no, my energy is just normal.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people could not?

Hear or see things? Like... imaginary things? No, definitely not. My vision and hearing are perfectly fine. 

I actually had my hearing tested back when I was taking classes at the community college. I was originally thinking about nursing before I settled on phlebotomy. Anatomy was such a tough class, mostly because the professor, Dr. Miller, mumbled the entire time. You really needed perfect hearing just to pass his tests. He always wore these awful, scratchy-looking sweater vests, too, even in the middle of May. I don't know how he didn't sweat to death, especially since the AC in the science building was broken for half the semester. The maintenance guy kept saying they were waiting on a part from Chicago, but it took forever. I remember sitting there just fanning myself with my notebook. 

But anyway... no. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I just see what is actually right in front of me, like what's really happening with my dad's chart. I'm not making things up in my head, if that's what you mean. I don't have hallucinations.
Have you been diagnosed with any brain or neurological illness?

Brain or neurological? Like... no, definitely not. My brain is completely fine. 

I did have a really awful headache last Thursday, though, if that's what you mean. It started right after my shift ended. I had to draw blood from this guy who had the most difficult rolling veins I've seen in months. We call them rollers in the clinic. You try to anchor the skin, but the vein just slides right out of the way of the needle. Plus, he was wearing this thick, bright orange hunting jacket that smelled exactly like wet dog, and it just lingered in the room. I really don't understand why people wear their dirty outdoor gear right into a clinical environment, you know? It's so inconsiderate. 

It actually reminded me of my old dog, Buster. He used to smell exactly like that after he'd jump into the creek behind my mom's house. We always had to hose him down on the patio before he could come inside, and my mom would get so mad because he'd shake muddy water all over her prize azalea bushes. She spent hours pruning those bushes every spring... wait, what did you ask me? 

Oh, right, brain illnesses. No, I don't have anything like that. The only people with something wrong with their heads are the ones altering my dad's lab results. But me? No, my brain is perfectly healthy.
Do people often tell you that your speech goes off track or is hard to follow?

Off track? No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever said that to me. I communicate very clearly. You have to in my job. 

Like yesterday, I had to explain the fasting requirements for a lipid panel to this older woman. She kept asking if black coffee counted as breaking the fast. I told her no, black coffee is fine, but you can't put any cream or sugar in it. And then she started going on about how she only uses that non-dairy powdered creamer, the kind that comes in the big plastic tub with the red lid. My grandma used to buy that exact same brand. She kept it in the pantry right next to the saltines. We used to eat saltines with peanut butter when we'd go over to her house on Sundays after church. My brother would always try to eat them whole and end up choking on the crumbs. He was always doing stupid stuff like that. He actually broke his arm once trying to jump off the roof of the garage onto a trampoline... 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, people don't tell me my speech is hard to follow. I think I'm pretty easy to understand.

Is it actually possible, in your view, for someone in the clinic system to change your dad’s lab results, or do you believe they are altering them in a way that ordinary people would think is impossible?

Is it possible? Of course it's possible. They just go into the computer system and change the numbers. It's not magic, it's just... data entry. Anyone with access to the Electronic Health Record can do it. 

I know how the EHR works because we use Epic at our clinic, too. The interface is actually really clunky. They did this massive software update last November, right before Thanksgiving, and it completely messed up the label printing for the blood tubes. We had to hand-write the accession numbers on the labels for three days. My hand was cramping so badly by the end of my shift. I had to go buy one of those wrist braces from the pharmacy. The pharmacist, Dave, he's such a nice guy. He always gives my kids a lollipop when we go in to pick up my son's asthma inhaler. My son loves the grape ones, but they always seem to run out of grape first. I don't know why they don't just order more grape if it's the most popular flavor. It's like the people who order the supplies don't even pay attention to what people actually want. Just like the people who order the butterfly needles at my work. They always order the 21-gauge instead of the 23-gauge, and the 21s are just too big for the older patients... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my dad's labs. Yeah, no, it's not impossible at all. It's just someone logging in and changing the potassium levels to make him look sicker than he is. It's very simple, really.
If someone showed you clear proof that your dad’s lab results had not been changed, would you be able to accept that?

Clear proof? I mean, what would that even look like? For the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I just... I can't just accept it, because I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s honestly wearing me down. 

My sister, Chloe, she's one of the ones who keeps telling me to just drop it and that the numbers are fine. She always does that, though. She just ignores problems until they go away. She was exactly like that when she was planning her wedding last spring. The caterer accidentally ordered regular pasta instead of gluten-free for the reception, and Chloe just shrugged it off, even though our cousin Mark has Celiac disease. Mark ended up having to eat nothing but the side salad and these dry dinner rolls he brought himself. He brings his own bread everywhere in these little plastic Tupperware containers. The ones with the blue snap-on lids? I used to use those to pack my lunches when I worked at the plasma center downtown. That place was always freezing cold. I had to wear a long-sleeve thermal shirt under my scrubs every single day, and the manager, Linda, she used to complain that my thermal wasn't the exact right shade of navy blue to match the company dress code. She was so obsessed with the dress code, but she never actually enforced the safety protocols for the centrifuge... 

Wait, what did you just ask me about? Oh, right, proof about the labs. Yeah, I mean, they can show me whatever they want, but I know what I saw. The numbers on that chart are wrong, and no one can convince me otherwise.
Over the past year, have you become much less interested in being around other people?

Less interested in being around people? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still go to work and see my patients every day. I'm around people all the time. 

Actually, we just had a potluck at the clinic last Friday for one of the medical assistants who was retiring. Brenda. She's been there for like, twenty-five years. I made my famous baked ziti. Everyone always asks for the recipe, but it's a secret my mom taught me. The trick is you have to mix a little bit of cream cheese into the ricotta before you layer it. It makes it so much richer. I buy the block cream cheese, not the spreadable kind in the tub. The tub kind has too much water in it, and it makes the sauce runny. I learned that the hard way when I made it for my son's baseball team banquet two years ago. The sauce was just a watery mess at the bottom of the aluminum pan. Those pans are so flimsy anyway. You always have to put a baking sheet underneath them or they buckle when you take them out of the oven. I burned my wrist on the oven rack doing that once. It left a scar that looks exactly like a crescent moon. My daughter thought it was a tattoo when she was little. She went through this phase where she wanted to draw tattoos on everyone with those washable markers. She drew a giant butterfly on my arm right before I had to go to the dentist...

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, being around people. Yeah, no, I'm fine being around people. I haven't noticed any change with that.
Have you noticed that your emotions feel flatter than they used to?

Flatter? No, I don't feel flat. I feel... well, I feel like I've always felt, really. I mean, I get upset about the lab results, obviously, but that's just normal when no one will listen to you. 

I definitely still have feelings. Like, I cried just the other day watching this commercial for dog food. It had this little golden retriever puppy that was trying to climb up the porch stairs, and his little legs were too short. It reminded me of the dog we had when I was growing up, Buster. He was a beagle mix, and he used to howl every time the mail truck drove by. Our mail carrier, Gary, he actually started carrying dog biscuits in his pocket just for Buster. Gary was great. He wore those funny little postal service shorts even when it was snowing out. I don't know how his legs didn't freeze. My legs get cold if I just look at the snow. I have to wear fleece-lined leggings under my jeans all winter. I buy them online in bulk because the ones at the store always pill up after two washes. The little fuzzballs drive me crazy. I bought one of those fabric shavers, you know, the ones that look like a little electric razor? It takes forever to do a whole pair of leggings, though. I usually end up doing it while I'm watching TV. I've been rewatching that old medical drama, the one from the early 2000s. It's so funny how inaccurate the blood draws are on that show. They never even tie the tourniquet tight enough...

Sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, about my emotions. Yeah, no, they're not flat. I feel perfectly normal.
Has anyone ever told you that your thoughts seem jumbled or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that is hard to follow?

Jumbled? No, I don't think my thoughts are jumbled. I mean, I know exactly what I'm talking about. People at work sometimes tell me to slow down when I'm explaining something, but that's just because I have a lot of details to get through. 

Especially when I'm training the new phlebotomists. We just hired this girl, Sarah, and she's sweet, but she has no idea how to properly label the vials. She always puts the barcode sticker on crooked, and then the scanner in the lab can't read it. The scanner is this old, clunky machine that looks like it's from the 1990s. It has this glowing red laser that always reminds me of those barcode scanners at the grocery store. My local grocery store just put in all new self-checkout lanes, and they are a nightmare. The bagging area is way too small. If you buy more than three things, the machine starts yelling at you to remove the items from the bagging area, but if you take them out, it yells at you to put them back. I was trying to buy a watermelon there last week, and it rolled right off the little scale and smashed on the floor. It was a huge mess. The manager had to come over with a mop, and it was one of those industrial string mops. I hate those. They never actually clean the floor; they just push the dirty water around. I use a steam mop at home. It gets the tile in my kitchen so clean you could eat off it. I have this beautiful Spanish-style tile with blue and yellow patterns...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my thoughts being jumbled. No, nobody's ever told me that. I think I make perfect sense.
Have you used any drugs or medications that you think might affect your mind?

Drugs? No, I don't use any drugs. Just my regular vitamins, and sometimes ibuprofen if I get a headache from the fluorescent lights at the clinic. Those lights are so harsh. They buzz, too. It's this low hum that you don't notice at first, but by the end of an eight-hour shift, it feels like it's vibrating right inside my teeth. 

I told the maintenance guy, Carl, about it. He said he'd change the bulbs, but he always says that. Carl is nice, though. He brings in donuts on Fridays from this little bakery near his house. They have the best apple fritters. They're huge, like the size of my head, and they have these big chunks of actual apple in them, not just that weird jelly stuff. I tried to make apple fritters at home once, but the oil got too hot and I burned the outside while the inside was still raw dough. Frying things is so tricky. I bought an air fryer to try and be healthier, but it just takes up so much counter space. I have a tiny kitchen in my apartment. The cabinets are this awful mustard yellow color from the seventies. I've been wanting to paint them white, but I'm worried I'll mess it up and the landlord will keep my security deposit. He's really strict about that stuff. He wouldn't even let me hang a picture without using those special command strips...

Wait, sorry. Drugs? No, I don't take anything like that. Just the vitamins.
When you’re talking, do other people ever have trouble following you because your answers drift onto unrelated topics?

Trouble following me? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm just having a normal conversation, right? Like, I just tell people what happened. It's not my fault if they can't keep up. My sister, Brenda, she always says I talk too fast, but she just has a short attention span. 

She's always been like that, even when we were kids. We used to share a bedroom, and she could never just sit still and read a book. She had to be doing a million things at once. We had bunk beds—I had the top bunk, obviously, because I was older. I loved being up high. I had these glow-in-the-dark stars stuck all over the ceiling right above my bed. You know, the plastic ones that come with that little sticky putty? The putty always dried out and eventually they'd just fall on my face in the middle of the night. It's funny how things that glow in the dark never actually glow for very long. Like those bracelets you get at concerts or fairs. I went to the state fair last summer and got a pink one. The fair was so crowded, though. The line for the Ferris wheel was at least an hour long. I didn't even go on it because heights make my stomach feel weird now. It's weird how your body changes as you get older. Like, I can't eat spicy food anymore without getting heartburn. I used to put hot sauce on everything. Eggs, pizza, even mac and cheese. There's this one brand with a rooster on the bottle... sriracha, yeah. I loved that stuff. But now, even mild salsa gives me acid reflux. I have to buy the kind that just tastes like crushed tomatoes. It's so boring. I tried making my own salsa once with just a tiny bit of jalapeño, but I rubbed my eye after cutting the pepper and it burned for like three hours. I had to hold a cold, wet paper towel over it...

Oh, wait. What did you ask me? About people following me when I talk? Yeah, no, I think I stay on topic just fine.
Have you ever felt that someone was putting thoughts into your mind or controlling your thoughts?

Putting thoughts in my mind? No, nobody can do that. That sounds like something out of a movie. I have my own thoughts, and they're perfectly fine. I don't need anyone else's. 

Like those sci-fi movies my ex-boyfriend used to watch. He was obsessed with them. He had this huge collection of DVDs, which took up a whole shelf in the living room. DVDs are so obsolete now, you know? Everything is streaming. I have a subscription to this one service, mostly just to watch this baking competition show. It's so relaxing. They make these incredible cakes that look like real objects, like a purse or a shoe. I don't know how they get the fondant so smooth. I tried using fondant once for my niece's birthday cake. It was supposed to be a unicorn, but the horn kept drooping and the fondant tasted like sweet plastic. The kids didn't care, though, they just ate the frosting. Frosting is the best part anyway. I like the kind that comes in a can, the chocolate fudge one. Sometimes I just eat a spoonful of it right out of the fridge when I need a quick sugar fix. The fridge in my apartment is always making this weird rattling noise, though. I think the ice maker is broken, but I don't even use ice that much. It waters down your drink too fast. Especially iced coffee. If I get iced coffee, I always ask for light ice, otherwise it's just brown water by the time I get to work. The coffee shop near the clinic has the best cold brew, though. They put this little splash of oat milk in it...

Wait, sorry. Controlling my thoughts? No, definitely not. Nobody is doing that.
Has anyone at work or at home told you that, when you talk, your ideas become so mixed up that they cannot understand what you mean?

Mixed up? No, I don't think my ideas are mixed up. I mean, I explain things exactly how they happen. If people don't understand, maybe they just aren't listening closely enough. People don't really listen anymore, you know? They just wait for their turn to talk. 

Like, I was trying to tell Brenda about this new patient at the clinic—well, not a new patient, but someone who hadn't been in for a while. He had these incredible veins, just right there on the surface, perfect for a blood draw. I love when that happens. Sometimes you get people who are so dehydrated you have to poke them twice, which I hate doing. It makes me feel terrible. I always tell them to drink plenty of water before they come in, but they never do. They always say they forgot or they drank coffee instead. Coffee actually dehydrates you, though. It's a diuretic. I learned that in my anatomy class back in college. I only took a few classes before I decided to do the phlebotomy certification instead. College was just so expensive, and I didn't want to take out all those loans. My cousin took out loans for a degree in art history, and now she works at a shoe store. She gets a great discount on shoes, though. She got me these really comfortable sneakers for work. They have memory foam insoles. Standing all day really does a number on your lower back. I tried doing yoga to help with it, but I just end up falling asleep during the relaxing part at the end. The instructor plays this soft flute music and turns the lights down...

But yeah, no. Nobody has told me they can't understand what I mean. I make perfect sense.
Have you had a head injury in the past year?

A head injury? No, not that I can remember. I haven't hit my head or anything. I mean, I'm pretty careful. 

Although, I did bump my elbow really hard on the edge of the centrifuge at work last week. It bruised up immediately. It was one of those really ugly, dark purple bruises that turns green and yellow after a few days. It's right on the funny bone, too, so it tingled all the way down to my pinky finger. I hate that feeling. It's like when your foot falls asleep because you've been sitting on it wrong. I do that all the time when I watch TV. I sit cross-legged on the couch, and then when I try to stand up, I have to hobble around for a minute until the pins and needles go away. My couch is really deep, though, so it's easy to just sink into it. It's this dark grey microfiber, which is supposed to be easy to clean, but it shows every single piece of lint. I have to use one of those sticky rollers on it constantly. I go through so many of those rolls. You can buy them in bulk at that big warehouse club. My mom has a membership there, and she always takes me with her so I can stock up on paper towels and stuff. They sell these massive muffins in the bakery section there. Like, they're the size of a grapefruit. I got the blueberry ones last time, but they put way too much sugar on top. It gets all crunchy and makes a mess everywhere when you take a bite. I ended up having to vacuum my car because I ate one on the way home. My car vacuum is just this little handheld thing that plugs into the cigarette lighter... well, they don't call it a cigarette lighter anymore, do they? It's a power outlet now. Nobody really smokes in their cars anymore. The smell just gets trapped in the upholstery...

But no, a head injury? Definitely not. I haven't had anything like that.
Has anyone ever told you that, at times, the words you say don’t fit together or come out so mixed up that they can’t understand you at all?

Words not fitting together? No, I don't think so. I mean, I speak English perfectly fine. Sometimes I talk a little fast if I'm excited, but people can understand me. I've never had anyone tell me I sounded mixed up. 

Although, there was this one time at the grocery store last week where the cashier couldn't understand me, but she had her headphones in. She was listening to something, maybe a podcast. I listen to a lot of podcasts when I'm cleaning the apartment. Mostly true crime ones. It's fascinating how they solve those cold cases using DNA now. It makes me think about all the blood samples I take at the clinic. Like, what if one of those people is secretly a criminal and their DNA gets put into a database? Not that we run DNA tests, we just do basic panels, cholesterol, A1C, that kind of thing. But it's crazy how much information is just floating around in your blood. My aunt got one of those ancestry kits for Christmas a few years ago, the ones where you spit in a tube. She found out she's like, two percent Scandinavian, which she thought was so exotic. She started buying all this lingonberry jam from IKEA. IKEA is so overwhelming, though. It's like a maze. You go in for a lamp and you end up leaving with three house plants and a bag of meatballs. The meatballs aren't even that good, they're kind of spongy. I prefer making my own with ground turkey. It's healthier, you know? Ground beef is so heavy, it always gives me heartburn if I eat it too late at night. I have to sleep propped up on two pillows if I eat red meat after 7 PM. My pillows are getting kind of flat, actually. I need to get new ones. Maybe bamboo ones? I heard those stay cool...

But no, nobody has ever told me my words don't fit together. I'm very clear when I speak.
Have the people close to you said that your personality has changed over the past year?

Personality changed? No, I don't think so. I'm exactly the same person I've always been. I mean, my mom says I'm working too much, but that's just because we've been short-staffed at the clinic. We had two girls quit in the same week. One of them moved to Texas because her husband got a job out there in the oil fields or something. I can't imagine living in Texas, it's way too hot. I sweat so much just walking from my car to the grocery store in the summer here. I have to carry one of those little travel deodorants in my purse. I buy the clinical strength kind, the one that clicks when you turn the dial at the bottom. It smells like baby powder, which I actually really like. It reminds me of my grandmother's house. She used to have this huge powder puff on her vanity that she'd use after her bath. Her vanity had this beautiful trifold mirror, the kind where you can see the back of your head if you angle it right. I've always wanted one of those so I could try doing French braids on myself. I can never get the back to look right, it always gets bumpy. I tried watching tutorials on YouTube, but they do it so fast. YouTube has a tutorial for literally everything now, though. I watched one last week on how to fix a leaky faucet because my kitchen sink was dripping and driving me crazy. It was just a worn-out washer, super easy to replace. You just need an Allen wrench. I have this little toolkit I keep under the sink that has a bunch of different sizes...

But yeah, my personality hasn't changed. I'm still just me.
Have you had any seizures?

Seizures? Oh, no, definitely not. I've never had a seizure or anything like that. I've never even fainted, actually. 

Although, I did get really dizzy once when I stood up too fast after donating blood. It was during that big community blood drive they do every summer at the high school gym. The gym always smells so strongly of floor wax and old sweat, it's just a very distinct smell. It reminds me of pep rallies when I was a teenager. I was in the marching band, I played the clarinet. We had these awful, heavy wool uniforms that were so itchy, especially during the August parades. We had to wear these tall hats with plumes on them, and they'd always blow off if it was windy. My friend Sarah lost her hat right in the middle of a routine once, and it rolled all the way down Main Street. Sarah's a real estate agent now, she sells these huge houses out in the suburbs. She showed me pictures of this one place that had a double oven in the kitchen. I would love a double oven. I tried to bake two sheets of cookies at once in my little oven last Christmas, and the bottom ones got completely burnt while the top ones were still raw in the middle. I had to throw the whole bottom batch out for the birds. The crows in my neighborhood are huge, they'll eat anything. They sit on the power lines and just watch you when you take the trash out. It's a little creepy, honestly. They're so smart, though. I read somewhere that crows can recognize human faces and remember if you were mean to them. So I always try to be nice and just leave them alone...

But anyway, no, I haven't had any seizures. I'm totally fine in that department.
Has anyone ever told you that, when you talk, your sentences become so disorganized that they can’t understand you at all?

I feel like you asked me something really similar a few minutes ago. But no, nobody has ever told me my sentences are disorganized. I make perfect sense. I have to be really clear at work, especially when I'm talking to the older patients at the clinic. Sometimes they can't hear very well, so I have to enunciate. And you have to write everything down clearly, too. We use these specific fine-tip markers for the blood tubes so the lab can read the patient names. I actually hide my favorite marker in my scrub pocket so the other girls don't take it. 

Scrubs are so comfortable, honestly. It's like wearing pajamas to work. I buy the ones with the extra cargo pockets on the side because I always need a place to keep my lip balm. I'm obsessed with this peppermint lip balm I found at a farmer's market last fall. The farmer's market is so nice, there's this one guy who sells the most amazing heirloom tomatoes. They're so ugly, like all lumpy and purple, but they taste incredible with just a little bit of salt and olive oil. Olive oil has gotten so expensive lately, though. I saw a tiny bottle at the store for like fifteen dollars the other day. It's ridiculous. I ended up just buying canola oil, even though they say it's not as good for you. You read so many different things about what's good for you and what isn't, it changes every week. One day coffee is bad, the next day it prevents heart disease. I try to just stick to one cup in the morning, otherwise I get the jitters. 

But anyway, no, my sentences don't get disorganized. People understand me perfectly.
Did this start soon after you began any new prescription medicine?

New prescription medicine? No, I haven't started anything new. I don't really take any prescriptions. I just go to the pharmacy for my vitamins, mostly. 

The drive-thru line at the pharmacy near my apartment is always so backed up, though. It spills right out onto the main road, so I usually just park and go inside because it's actually faster. Plus, then I can look at the greeting cards while I wait. I had to get a birthday card for my niece last week, she just turned seven. Greeting cards are getting so expensive now, it's honestly crazy. I paid almost eight dollars for one that played a little song when you open it. It played that "Walking on Sunshine" song. It's a catchy song, but it gets stuck in your head all day. I actually heard it playing on the radio at the dentist's office a few months ago. I hate going to the dentist. The sound of that little metal scraper tool just goes right through me, it makes my teeth ache just thinking about it. My hygienist is really nice, though, her name is Brenda and she always gives me a free travel toothpaste and a toothbrush. I only use soft-bristle brushes because the medium ones hurt my gums. I read an article that said you're actually supposed to brush really gently, like you're polishing a tomato, which is a weird comparison but I guess it makes sense. Tomatoes bruise so easily. I tried growing them in a pot on my balcony last summer, but the squirrels kept taking exactly one bite out of the red ones and just leaving them on the railing. They are such menaces. 

But no, I'm not taking any new medicines. Just my regular vitamins.

I actually bought this new weighted blanket recently to help me get comfortable at night, because sometimes it takes me a while to drift off just thinking about my dad's situation. And when the delivery guy finally brought it, he just left it right in the middle of my driveway. Didn't even bring it up to the porch. Anyone could have just driven by and taken it. patient.answer:
Hear or see things? Like... imaginary things? No, definitely not. My vision and hearing are perfectly fine. 

I actually had my hearing tested back when I was taking classes at the community college. I was originally thinking about nursing before I settled on phlebotomy. Anatomy was such a tough class, mostly because the professor, Dr. Miller, mumbled the entire time. You really needed perfect hearing just to pass his tests. He always wore these awful, scratchy-looking sweater vests, too, even in the middle of May. I don't know how he didn't sweat to death, especially since the AC in the science building was broken for half the semester. The maintenance guy kept saying they were waiting on a part from Chicago, but it took forever. I remember sitting there just fanning myself with my notebook. 

But anyway... no. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I just see what is actually right in front of me, like what's really happening with my dad's chart. I'm not making things up in my head, if that's what you mean. I don't have hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Brain or neurological? Like... no, definitely not. My brain is completely fine. 

I did have a really awful headache last Thursday, though, if that's what you mean. It started right after my shift ended. I had to draw blood from this guy who had the most difficult rolling veins I've seen in months. We call them rollers in the clinic. You try to anchor the skin, but the vein just slides right out of the way of the needle. Plus, he was wearing this thick, bright orange hunting jacket that smelled exactly like wet dog, and it just lingered in the room. I really don't understand why people wear their dirty outdoor gear right into a clinical environment, you know? It's so inconsiderate. 

It actually reminded me of my old dog, Buster. He used to smell exactly like that after he'd jump into the creek behind my mom's house. We always had to hose him down on the patio before he could come inside, and my mom would get so mad because he'd shake muddy water all over her prize azalea bushes. She spent hours pruning those bushes every spring... wait, what did you ask me? 

Oh, right, brain illnesses. No, I don't have anything like that. The only people with something wrong with their heads are the ones altering my dad's lab results. But me? No, my brain is perfectly healthy.

Off track? No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever said that to me. I communicate very clearly. You have to in my job. 

Like yesterday, I had to explain the fasting requirements for a lipid panel to this older woman. She kept asking if black coffee counted as breaking the fast. I told her no, black coffee is fine, but you can't put any cream or sugar in it. And then she started going on about how she only uses that non-dairy powdered creamer, the kind that comes in the big plastic tub with the red lid. My grandma used to buy that exact same brand. She kept it in the pantry right next to the saltines. We used to eat saltines with peanut butter when we'd go over to her house on Sundays after church. My brother would always try to eat them whole and end up choking on the crumbs. He was always doing stupid stuff like that. He actually broke his arm once trying to jump off the roof of the garage onto a trampoline... 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, people don't tell me my speech is hard to follow. I think I'm pretty easy to understand.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed belief about the father’s lab results is bizarre/impossible versus potentially understandable, which best separates delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the plausibility of the delusion (whether it's bizarre or non-bizarre). The symptom profile for 'Delusions' describes the fixed belief about the lab results but does not explicitly address the doctor's specific question about whether the patient believes the alteration is happening in a way ordinary people would think is impossible (bizarre vs non-bizarre delusion specifier).

patient.answer:
Is it possible? Of course it's possible. They just go into the computer system and change the numbers. It's not magic, it's just... data entry. Anyone with access to the Electronic Health Record can do it. 

I know how the EHR works because we use Epic at our clinic, too. The interface is actually really clunky. They did this massive software update last November, right before Thanksgiving, and it completely messed up the label printing for the blood tubes. We had to hand-write the accession numbers on the labels for three days. My hand was cramping so badly by the end of my shift. I had to go buy one of those wrist braces from the pharmacy. The pharmacist, Dave, he's such a nice guy. He always gives my kids a lollipop when we go in to pick up my son's asthma inhaler. My son loves the grape ones, but they always seem to run out of grape first. I don't know why they don't just order more grape if it's the most popular flavor. It's like the people who order the supplies don't even pay attention to what people actually want. Just like the people who order the butterfly needles at my work. They always order the 21-gauge instead of the 23-gauge, and the 21s are just too big for the older patients... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my dad's labs. Yeah, no, it's not impossible at all. It's just someone logging in and changing the potassium levels to make him look sicker than he is. It's very simple, really.

Clear proof? I mean, what would that even look like? For the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I just... I can't just accept it, because I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s honestly wearing me down. 

My sister, Chloe, she's one of the ones who keeps telling me to just drop it and that the numbers are fine. She always does that, though. She just ignores problems until they go away. She was exactly like that when she was planning her wedding last spring. The caterer accidentally ordered regular pasta instead of gluten-free for the reception, and Chloe just shrugged it off, even though our cousin Mark has Celiac disease. Mark ended up having to eat nothing but the side salad and these dry dinner rolls he brought himself. He brings his own bread everywhere in these little plastic Tupperware containers. The ones with the blue snap-on lids? I used to use those to pack my lunches when I worked at the plasma center downtown. That place was always freezing cold. I had to wear a long-sleeve thermal shirt under my scrubs every single day, and the manager, Linda, she used to complain that my thermal wasn't the exact right shade of navy blue to match the company dress code. She was so obsessed with the dress code, but she never actually enforced the safety protocols for the centrifuge... 

Wait, what did you just ask me about? Oh, right, proof about the labs. Yeah, I mean, they can show me whatever they want, but I know what I saw. The numbers on that chart are wrong, and no one can convince me otherwise.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia over persistent delusional disorder or acute psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Over the past year, have you become much less interested in being around other people?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a decrease in interest in socializing or being around other people (avolition/asociality, negative symptoms of schizophrenia). This is not covered by any of my symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Less interested in being around people? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still go to work and see my patients every day. I'm around people all the time. 

Actually, we just had a potluck at the clinic last Friday for one of the medical assistants who was retiring. Brenda. She's been there for like, twenty-five years. I made my famous baked ziti. Everyone always asks for the recipe, but it's a secret my mom taught me. The trick is you have to mix a little bit of cream cheese into the ricotta before you layer it. It makes it so much richer. I buy the block cream cheese, not the spreadable kind in the tub. The tub kind has too much water in it, and it makes the sauce runny. I learned that the hard way when I made it for my son's baseball team banquet two years ago. The sauce was just a watery mess at the bottom of the aluminum pan. Those pans are so flimsy anyway. You always have to put a baking sheet underneath them or they buckle when you take them out of the oven. I burned my wrist on the oven rack doing that once. It left a scar that looks exactly like a crescent moon. My daughter thought it was a tattoo when she was little. She went through this phase where she wanted to draw tattoos on everyone with those washable markers. She drew a giant butterfly on my arm right before I had to go to the dentist...

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, being around people. Yeah, no, I'm fine being around people. I haven't noticed any change with that.

patient.answer:
Flatter? No, I don't feel flat. I feel... well, I feel like I've always felt, really. I mean, I get upset about the lab results, obviously, but that's just normal when no one will listen to you. 

I definitely still have feelings. Like, I cried just the other day watching this commercial for dog food. It had this little golden retriever puppy that was trying to climb up the porch stairs, and his little legs were too short. It reminded me of the dog we had when I was growing up, Buster. He was a beagle mix, and he used to howl every time the mail truck drove by. Our mail carrier, Gary, he actually started carrying dog biscuits in his pocket just for Buster. Gary was great. He wore those funny little postal service shorts even when it was snowing out. I don't know how his legs didn't freeze. My legs get cold if I just look at the snow. I have to wear fleece-lined leggings under my jeans all winter. I buy them online in bulk because the ones at the store always pill up after two washes. The little fuzzballs drive me crazy. I bought one of those fabric shavers, you know, the ones that look like a little electric razor? It takes forever to do a whole pair of leggings, though. I usually end up doing it while I'm watching TV. I've been rewatching that old medical drama, the one from the early 2000s. It's so funny how inaccurate the blood draws are on that show. They never even tie the tourniquet tight enough...

Sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, about my emotions. Yeah, no, they're not flat. I feel perfectly normal.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are accompanied by formal thought disorder/disorganized speech, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or an organic delusional disorder.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized thinking or speech (jumbled thoughts, jumping from one idea to another), which is a symptom of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders. My symptom profile does not contain an item for disorganized speech or thought processes.

patient.answer:
Jumbled? No, I don't think my thoughts are jumbled. I mean, I know exactly what I'm talking about. People at work sometimes tell me to slow down when I'm explaining something, but that's just because I have a lot of details to get through. 

Especially when I'm training the new phlebotomists. We just hired this girl, Sarah, and she's sweet, but she has no idea how to properly label the vials. She always puts the barcode sticker on crooked, and then the scanner in the lab can't read it. The scanner is this old, clunky machine that looks like it's from the 1990s. It has this glowing red laser that always reminds me of those barcode scanners at the grocery store. My local grocery store just put in all new self-checkout lanes, and they are a nightmare. The bagging area is way too small. If you buy more than three things, the machine starts yelling at you to remove the items from the bagging area, but if you take them out, it yells at you to put them back. I was trying to buy a watermelon there last week, and it rolled right off the little scale and smashed on the floor. It was a huge mess. The manager had to come over with a mop, and it was one of those industrial string mops. I hate those. They never actually clean the floor; they just push the dirty water around. I use a steam mop at home. It gets the tile in my kitchen so clean you could eat off it. I have this beautiful Spanish-style tile with blue and yellow patterns...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my thoughts being jumbled. No, nobody's ever told me that. I think I make perfect sense.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a history of substance use or medication exposure that could explain the psychotic symptoms, helping distinguish an organic/substance-induced psychotic disorder from primary psychotic disorders.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about substance use or medications that might affect the mind, which is not covered by any of the symptom profiles provided.

patient.answer:
Drugs? No, I don't use any drugs. Just my regular vitamins, and sometimes ibuprofen if I get a headache from the fluorescent lights at the clinic. Those lights are so harsh. They buzz, too. It's this low hum that you don't notice at first, but by the end of an eight-hour shift, it feels like it's vibrating right inside my teeth. 

I told the maintenance guy, Carl, about it. He said he'd change the bulbs, but he always says that. Carl is nice, though. He brings in donuts on Fridays from this little bakery near his house. They have the best apple fritters. They're huge, like the size of my head, and they have these big chunks of actual apple in them, not just that weird jelly stuff. I tried to make apple fritters at home once, but the oil got too hot and I burned the outside while the inside was still raw dough. Frying things is so tricky. I bought an air fryer to try and be healthier, but it just takes up so much counter space. I have a tiny kitchen in my apartment. The cabinets are this awful mustard yellow color from the seventies. I've been wanting to paint them white, but I'm worried I'll mess it up and the landlord will keep my security deposit. He's really strict about that stuff. He wouldn't even let me hang a picture without using those special command strips...

Wait, sorry. Drugs? No, I don't take anything like that. Just the vitamins.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are accompanied by prominent formal thought disorder/disorganized speech observable outside the patient’s self-report, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder or an organic delusional disorder.
doctor.question: When you’re talking, do other people ever have trouble following you because your answers drift onto unrelated topics?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about tangential speech or drifting onto unrelated topics (derailment/tangentiality), which is a symptom of disorganized speech, often seen in schizophrenia. This is not covered by my symptom profile for Delusional Disorder.

patient.answer:
Trouble following me? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm just having a normal conversation, right? Like, I just tell people what happened. It's not my fault if they can't keep up. My sister, Brenda, she always says I talk too fast, but she just has a short attention span. 

She's always been like that, even when we were kids. We used to share a bedroom, and she could never just sit still and read a book. She had to be doing a million things at once. We had bunk beds—I had the top bunk, obviously, because I was older. I loved being up high. I had these glow-in-the-dark stars stuck all over the ceiling right above my bed. You know, the plastic ones that come with that little sticky putty? The putty always dried out and eventually they'd just fall on my face in the middle of the night. It's funny how things that glow in the dark never actually glow for very long. Like those bracelets you get at concerts or fairs. I went to the state fair last summer and got a pink one. The fair was so crowded, though. The line for the Ferris wheel was at least an hour long. I didn't even go on it because heights make my stomach feel weird now. It's weird how your body changes as you get older. Like, I can't eat spicy food anymore without getting heartburn. I used to put hot sauce on everything. Eggs, pizza, even mac and cheese. There's this one brand with a rooster on the bottle... sriracha, yeah. I loved that stuff. But now, even mild salsa gives me acid reflux. I have to buy the kind that just tastes like crushed tomatoes. It's so boring. I tried making my own salsa once with just a tiny bit of jalapeño, but I rubbed my eye after cutting the pepper and it burned for like three hours. I had to hold a cold, wet paper towel over it...

Oh, wait. What did you ask me? About people following me when I talk? Yeah, no, I think I stay on topic just fine.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent Schneiderian first-rank symptoms, especially thought insertion, broadcasting, or control, to distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and organic delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that someone was putting thoughts into your mind or controlling your thoughts?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion or thought control (delusions of control), which is not covered by any of the items in the symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Putting thoughts in my mind? No, nobody can do that. That sounds like something out of a movie. I have my own thoughts, and they're perfectly fine. I don't need anyone else's. 

Like those sci-fi movies my ex-boyfriend used to watch. He was obsessed with them. He had this huge collection of DVDs, which took up a whole shelf in the living room. DVDs are so obsolete now, you know? Everything is streaming. I have a subscription to this one service, mostly just to watch this baking competition show. It's so relaxing. They make these incredible cakes that look like real objects, like a purse or a shoe. I don't know how they get the fondant so smooth. I tried using fondant once for my niece's birthday cake. It was supposed to be a unicorn, but the horn kept drooping and the fondant tasted like sweet plastic. The kids didn't care, though, they just ate the frosting. Frosting is the best part anyway. I like the kind that comes in a can, the chocolate fudge one. Sometimes I just eat a spoonful of it right out of the fridge when I need a quick sugar fix. The fridge in my apartment is always making this weird rattling noise, though. I think the ice maker is broken, but I don't even use ice that much. It waters down your drink too fast. Especially iced coffee. If I get iced coffee, I always ask for light ice, otherwise it's just brown water by the time I get to work. The coffee shop near the clinic has the best cold brew, though. They put this little splash of oat milk in it...

Wait, sorry. Controlling my thoughts? No, definitely not. Nobody is doing that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are accompanied by a prominent formal thought disorder, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or an organic delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Has anyone at work or at home told you that, when you talk, your ideas become so mixed up that they cannot understand what you mean?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech (incoherence or word salad), which is a symptom of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders, but this is not present in my symptom profile (Delusional Disorder).

patient.answer:
Mixed up? No, I don't think my ideas are mixed up. I mean, I explain things exactly how they happen. If people don't understand, maybe they just aren't listening closely enough. People don't really listen anymore, you know? They just wait for their turn to talk. 

Like, I was trying to tell Brenda about this new patient at the clinic—well, not a new patient, but someone who hadn't been in for a while. He had these incredible veins, just right there on the surface, perfect for a blood draw. I love when that happens. Sometimes you get people who are so dehydrated you have to poke them twice, which I hate doing. It makes me feel terrible. I always tell them to drink plenty of water before they come in, but they never do. They always say they forgot or they drank coffee instead. Coffee actually dehydrates you, though. It's a diuretic. I learned that in my anatomy class back in college. I only took a few classes before I decided to do the phlebotomy certification instead. College was just so expensive, and I didn't want to take out all those loans. My cousin took out loans for a degree in art history, and now she works at a shoe store. She gets a great discount on shoes, though. She got me these really comfortable sneakers for work. They have memory foam insoles. Standing all day really does a number on your lower back. I tried doing yoga to help with it, but I just end up falling asleep during the relaxing part at the end. The instructor plays this soft flute music and turns the lights down...

But yeah, no. Nobody has told me they can't understand what I mean. I make perfect sense.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed persecutory belief is due to a medical condition by assessing for recent head injury, which best separates delusional disorder/paranoid schizophrenia from organic psychosis at this point.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of head injury in the past year, which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
A head injury? No, not that I can remember. I haven't hit my head or anything. I mean, I'm pretty careful. 

Although, I did bump my elbow really hard on the edge of the centrifuge at work last week. It bruised up immediately. It was one of those really ugly, dark purple bruises that turns green and yellow after a few days. It's right on the funny bone, too, so it tingled all the way down to my pinky finger. I hate that feeling. It's like when your foot falls asleep because you've been sitting on it wrong. I do that all the time when I watch TV. I sit cross-legged on the couch, and then when I try to stand up, I have to hobble around for a minute until the pins and needles go away. My couch is really deep, though, so it's easy to just sink into it. It's this dark grey microfiber, which is supposed to be easy to clean, but it shows every single piece of lint. I have to use one of those sticky rollers on it constantly. I go through so many of those rolls. You can buy them in bulk at that big warehouse club. My mom has a membership there, and she always takes me with her so I can stock up on paper towels and stuff. They sell these massive muffins in the bakery section there. Like, they're the size of a grapefruit. I got the blueberry ones last time, but they put way too much sugar on top. It gets all crunchy and makes a mess everywhere when you take a bite. I ended up having to vacuum my car because I ate one on the way home. My car vacuum is just this little handheld thing that plugs into the cigarette lighter... well, they don't call it a cigarette lighter anymore, do they? It's a power outlet now. Nobody really smokes in their cars anymore. The smell just gets trapped in the upholstery...

But no, a head injury? Definitely not. I haven't had anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is prominent thought disorganization/incoherent speech, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder and help distinguish primary psychosis from an organic delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Has anyone ever told you that, at times, the words you say don’t fit together or come out so mixed up that they can’t understand you at all?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech/word salad (words not fitting together or being completely mixed up so they cannot be understood). This is a symptom of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders, but it is not part of my symptom profile for Delusional Disorder.

patient.answer:
Words not fitting together? No, I don't think so. I mean, I speak English perfectly fine. Sometimes I talk a little fast if I'm excited, but people can understand me. I've never had anyone tell me I sounded mixed up. 

Although, there was this one time at the grocery store last week where the cashier couldn't understand me, but she had her headphones in. She was listening to something, maybe a podcast. I listen to a lot of podcasts when I'm cleaning the apartment. Mostly true crime ones. It's fascinating how they solve those cold cases using DNA now. It makes me think about all the blood samples I take at the clinic. Like, what if one of those people is secretly a criminal and their DNA gets put into a database? Not that we run DNA tests, we just do basic panels, cholesterol, A1C, that kind of thing. But it's crazy how much information is just floating around in your blood. My aunt got one of those ancestry kits for Christmas a few years ago, the ones where you spit in a tube. She found out she's like, two percent Scandinavian, which she thought was so exotic. She started buying all this lingonberry jam from IKEA. IKEA is so overwhelming, though. It's like a maze. You go in for a lamp and you end up leaving with three house plants and a bag of meatballs. The meatballs aren't even that good, they're kind of spongy. I prefer making my own with ground turkey. It's healthier, you know? Ground beef is so heavy, it always gives me heartburn if I eat it too late at night. I have to sleep propped up on two pillows if I eat red meat after 7 PM. My pillows are getting kind of flat, actually. I need to get new ones. Maybe bamboo ones? I heard those stay cool...

But no, nobody has ever told me my words don't fit together. I'm very clear when I speak.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a clear change in personality or behavior from her usual baseline, which would help distinguish a primary psychotic disorder from an organic psychosis.
doctor.question: Have the people close to you said that your personality has changed over the past year?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a change in personality over the past year, which is typically a screening question for organic causes or general behavioral changes. None of the symptom profile items (Delusions, Additional Requirement 1, Functional Impairment, Duration) specifically address a change in personality reported by close people.

patient.answer:
Personality changed? No, I don't think so. I'm exactly the same person I've always been. I mean, my mom says I'm working too much, but that's just because we've been short-staffed at the clinic. We had two girls quit in the same week. One of them moved to Texas because her husband got a job out there in the oil fields or something. I can't imagine living in Texas, it's way too hot. I sweat so much just walking from my car to the grocery store in the summer here. I have to carry one of those little travel deodorants in my purse. I buy the clinical strength kind, the one that clicks when you turn the dial at the bottom. It smells like baby powder, which I actually really like. It reminds me of my grandmother's house. She used to have this huge powder puff on her vanity that she'd use after her bath. Her vanity had this beautiful trifold mirror, the kind where you can see the back of your head if you angle it right. I've always wanted one of those so I could try doing French braids on myself. I can never get the back to look right, it always gets bumpy. I tried watching tutorials on YouTube, but they do it so fast. YouTube has a tutorial for literally everything now, though. I watched one last week on how to fix a leaky faucet because my kitchen sink was dripping and driving me crazy. It was just a worn-out washer, super easy to replace. You just need an Allen wrench. I have this little toolkit I keep under the sink that has a bunch of different sizes...

But yeah, my personality hasn't changed. I'm still just me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is evidence of a general medical cause for the psychosis, especially recent seizure-like episodes that would support an organic delusional disorder (F06.2) over primary psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you had any seizures?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about seizures, which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Seizures? Oh, no, definitely not. I've never had a seizure or anything like that. I've never even fainted, actually. 

Although, I did get really dizzy once when I stood up too fast after donating blood. It was during that big community blood drive they do every summer at the high school gym. The gym always smells so strongly of floor wax and old sweat, it's just a very distinct smell. It reminds me of pep rallies when I was a teenager. I was in the marching band, I played the clarinet. We had these awful, heavy wool uniforms that were so itchy, especially during the August parades. We had to wear these tall hats with plumes on them, and they'd always blow off if it was windy. My friend Sarah lost her hat right in the middle of a routine once, and it rolled all the way down Main Street. Sarah's a real estate agent now, she sells these huge houses out in the suburbs. She showed me pictures of this one place that had a double oven in the kitchen. I would love a double oven. I tried to bake two sheets of cookies at once in my little oven last Christmas, and the bottom ones got completely burnt while the top ones were still raw in the middle. I had to throw the whole bottom batch out for the birds. The crows in my neighborhood are huge, they'll eat anything. They sit on the power lines and just watch you when you take the trash out. It's a little creepy, honestly. They're so smart, though. I read somewhere that crows can recognize human faces and remember if you were mean to them. So I always try to be nice and just leave them alone...

But anyway, no, I haven't had any seizures. I'm totally fine in that department.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there is prominent formal thought disorder/disorganized speech, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or psychotic disorder due to a medical condition.
doctor.question: Has anyone ever told you that, when you talk, your sentences become so disorganized that they can’t understand you at all?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech (incoherence/word salad), which is a symptom of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders. My symptom profile only covers Delusions, Additional Requirement 1 (functioning not markedly impaired), Functional Impairment, and Duration. Therefore, I do not have a symptom profile item for disorganized speech.

patient.answer:
I feel like you asked me something really similar a few minutes ago. But no, nobody has ever told me my sentences are disorganized. I make perfect sense. I have to be really clear at work, especially when I'm talking to the older patients at the clinic. Sometimes they can't hear very well, so I have to enunciate. And you have to write everything down clearly, too. We use these specific fine-tip markers for the blood tubes so the lab can read the patient names. I actually hide my favorite marker in my scrub pocket so the other girls don't take it. 

Scrubs are so comfortable, honestly. It's like wearing pajamas to work. I buy the ones with the extra cargo pockets on the side because I always need a place to keep my lip balm. I'm obsessed with this peppermint lip balm I found at a farmer's market last fall. The farmer's market is so nice, there's this one guy who sells the most amazing heirloom tomatoes. They're so ugly, like all lumpy and purple, but they taste incredible with just a little bit of salt and olive oil. Olive oil has gotten so expensive lately, though. I saw a tiny bottle at the store for like fifteen dollars the other day. It's ridiculous. I ended up just buying canola oil, even though they say it's not as good for you. You read so many different things about what's good for you and what isn't, it changes every week. One day coffee is bad, the next day it prevents heart disease. I try to just stick to one cup in the morning, otherwise I get the jitters. 

But anyway, no, my sentences don't get disorganized. People understand me perfectly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a medical or substance-related cause for the psychotic symptoms by checking for a temporal link to starting a medication.
doctor.question: Did this start soon after you began any new prescription medicine?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms started after beginning a new prescription medication, which is a question about substance/medication-induced etiology. This is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
New prescription medicine? No, I haven't started anything new. I don't really take any prescriptions. I just go to the pharmacy for my vitamins, mostly. 

The drive-thru line at the pharmacy near my apartment is always so backed up, though. It spills right out onto the main road, so I usually just park and go inside because it's actually faster. Plus, then I can look at the greeting cards while I wait. I had to get a birthday card for my niece last week, she just turned seven. Greeting cards are getting so expensive now, it's honestly crazy. I paid almost eight dollars for one that played a little song when you open it. It played that "Walking on Sunshine" song. It's a catchy song, but it gets stuck in your head all day. I actually heard it playing on the radio at the dentist's office a few months ago. I hate going to the dentist. The sound of that little metal scraper tool just goes right through me, it makes my teeth ache just thinking about it. My hygienist is really nice, though, her name is Brenda and she always gives me a free travel toothpaste and a toothbrush. I only use soft-bristle brushes because the medium ones hurt my gums. I read an article that said you're actually supposed to brush really gently, like you're polishing a tomato, which is a weird comparison but I guess it makes sense. Tomatoes bruise so easily. I tried growing them in a pot on my balcony last summer, but the squirrels kept taking exactly one bite out of the red ones and just leaving them on the railing. They are such menaces. 

But no, I'm not taking any new medicines. Just my regular vitamins.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent, fixed persecutory-type delusional belief for about one year that clinic staff are altering her father's lab results, despite repeated contradiction by doctors and family and inability to accept disconfirming evidence. Hallucinations, thought insertion/control, negative symptoms, prominent social withdrawal, manic symptoms, substance/medication causes, and neurological illness are denied. Although the interview shows circumstantial and tangential speech, there is no clear evidence of the sustained psychotic disorganization or broader symptom constellation required for schizophrenia, and no evidence of an organic etiology.
